rounded.context: However, we identify a misalignment between translation-specific and general understanding in LLMs: models can mistranslate or translate literally complicated concepts that they understand correctly in general scenarios, such as QA (§6).

On the self-constructed Challenge-WMT1 benchmark, which comprises samples prone to mistranslation, human evaluation across high-resource and low-resource language pairs suggests that DUAT improves translation quality by up to +3.85 COMET and reduces translation literality by -25\% $\sim$-51\% (§6).

To address this gap, we propose DUAT (Difficult words Understanding Aligned Translation), which incorporates general understanding of complicated content into translation; on the evaluated settings, DUAT improves translation quality by up to +3.85 COMET and reduces translation literality by -25\% $\sim$-51\% (§6).
This design aims to help the model develop a deeper understanding of the source sentence and produce more nuanced translations (§6).
This alignment is also associated with improved automatic-metric scores, including up to +3.85 COMET, and lower translation literalness of -25\% $\sim$-51\% (§6).

Human evaluation on high-resource and low-resource language pairs shows that DUAT reduces generalization failures and improves translation quality by up to +3.85 COMET, while reducing translation literalness by -25\% $\sim$-51\% (§6).

We show that, on Challenge-WMT and the evaluated high-resource and low-resource language pairs, DUAT reduces 80\%$\sim$88\% of generalization failures, improves automatic translation metrics by up to +3.85 COMET, and reduces translation literalness by -25\% $\sim$-51\% (§6).
This design is intended to help the model better understand the source sentence and produce more nuanced translations (§6).

We further adapt token-level quality estimation (QE) from Rei et al. (2023) to improve difficult-word detection and design an interpretation quality-control strategy that uses sentence-level QE from Rei et al. (2020) to filter hallucinated interpretations (§6).
Human evaluation indicates that DUAT reduces 80\%$\sim$88\% of generalization failures (§6).
This alignment is also associated with improved translation quality, as measured by automatic metrics of up to +3.85 COMET, and reduced translation literalness of -25\% $\sim$-51\% (§6).
